post.summary: Check or save competitors, plans and plan features from a CSV or Excel file
post.description: The body is the file itself (.csv or .xlsx, up to 25 MB), not JSON. Columns are matched by meaning (Competitor, Tier, Module, Product, Plan, Level, Licence, Max users, Monthly / Yearly / Lifetime price, Currency, GST included, Features, Feature, Included), so most exported sheets work as they are. With commit=0 nothing is saved and the answer lists what would be created, what already exists, what was assumed and which rows were skipped. With commit=1 it is saved. Names are matched to existing ones ignoring case and punctuation, so importing twice adds nothing twice. Existing values are only filled in when blank, unless overwrite=1. Title lines above the column names are skipped; a plan name ending in a term ("Silver - 3 Month", "Gold - Lifetime") becomes one plan with several prices; a CSV saved by Excel on Windows (Windows-1252) is read correctly; a table with Tier 1/2/3 headings and a Modules column records which module each competitor competes in. Also answers at its old address /api/competitors/import, which is deprecated and ends on the Sunset date. Errors use the same envelope as the rest of /api/v1.

canDecideIdeas.description: The screens use this to show or hide the accept / reject buttons.

message.description: What went wrong, as the browser reported it.

digest.description: Next.js's short code for a server-side render error.

request_id.description: The request id the server gave the failed call, when there was one.

total.description: How many ideas match in all (not only on this page).

next.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page; null when this is the last one.

name.description: Product name (defaults to the idea line).

reason.description: Why the idea is turned down; kept with the idea and shown to the person who submitted it.

note.description: One plain line under the number.

href.description: Web route to open for the detail behind the number.

kind.description: software, hardware or service: which lifecycle template the product follows.

phase.description: The lifecycle phase (0 to 12) the product is in now.

staleValues.description: Facts that are out of date or due for a second look.

minutesOwed.description: Minutes of people's time still needed for the listed work.

owners.description: Distinct owners across the portfolio, for the filter box.

truncated.description: True when more than 500 events matched and the list was cut.

slug.description: The name used in web addresses.

category.description: Sponsor, Delivery, Customer, End-user, Partner, Regulator/Legal, Security/Privacy, Operations, Finance or Commercial (anything else becomes Delivery).

role_title.description: What they do, in their own words.

stage.description: Ask for every row of this stage that can be asked now (0-4).

row.description: Or ask for just this one row.

id.description: Keep the id of a step that already exists; leave it out for a new step.

text.description: What happens in this step, in a few words.

next.description: What happens next: auto (the next step in the list), end, or the id of another step.

fail.description: What happens when it fails: { text, condition?, test }.

steps.description: The whole list of steps, in order. At least one is needed.

text.description: What is wrong, in a few words (up to 4,000 characters).

categories.description: confusing, missing, broken, too much text.

route.description: The page the person was on.

product.description: Product id, when the note is about one product.

done.description: true (the default) ticks the note as dealt with, false un-ticks it.

name.description: The person's name, as it should be shown.

role.description: Owner, Lead, Contributor, Reviewer or Viewer (the default is Contributor).

scope.description: Where the person is added: the whole platform, one project, or one phase of a project.

product_id.description: The product id (such as PRD-001). Needed for "project" and "phase".

phase.description: The phase number, 0 to 12. Needed for "phase".

role.description: Owner, Lead, Contributor, Reviewer or Viewer.

by.description: Who is making the change (a named person, never an agent). Defaults to the person acting.

role.description: Their role, for example Product Owner or Sponsor.

request.description: The request this status change answers, when it comes from an approval.

second_approver.description: A second person's name, when the document needs two approvers.

waiver.description: An exception when the document is below the approval threshold: { reason, approver }.

rules.description: The rules the story must follow.

tests.description: How the story will be tested.

approver.description: Who is asked to approve the story.

story.description: The story whose package is delivered.

depth_level.description: L1, L2 or L3: how thorough the process is for this product.

asOf.description: Pretend today is this date (YYYY-MM-DD); empty goes back to the real date.

suspectDepth.description: How many steps a change travels when the tool marks work as needing a second look (1 to 5).

step.description: Step id such as P5.3. Send together with `tier`.

tier.description: core, major, support or light: how much the step counts toward its phase.

points.description: Points per level, for example { core: 10 }.

reset.description: Put the framework's own weights back.

origin.description: human or document; anything else counts as human.

reviewed.description: Mark that a person looked at the change (used for work the tool drafted).

expected_rev.description: The revision the caller was looking at. A different current revision gives 409 stale_edit.

name.description: The product's name. It must be unique among live products.

depth_level.description: How thorough the process is: L1, L2 or L3.

structure.description: single (one product) or modules (a suite whose modules each have their own competitors).

stage.description: A stage to hold the product in, or "auto" (or null) to let the tool decide.

idea.description: The idea behind it: { who_for, why_now, asked_by }.

text.description: The words of a file that could not be read, typed or pasted by a person.

competitor_id.description: Which competitor the suggestions belong to, when the file is not already attached to one.

own_product.description: The file describes the person's own product, not a competitor.

overwrite.description: Replace values that are already set.

candidates.description: The candidates the person chose from the suggestions: { id?, kind, fields, location, snippet, confidence, competitor_id?, overrides? }.

goal.description: What the assistant should look for (see the goals the file page offers).

target.description: The record the proposals are about, when the goal needs one.

confirm_cost.description: Live mode only: the person saw the estimated cost and agreed to it.

cap_inr.description: The most the paid assistant may cost in a month, in rupees. 0 switches it off.

overwrite.description: Replace values that are already set.

fields.description: The values to change; an empty value removes an optional field.

attachment.description: The attachment (file) the evidence comes from.

locator.description: Where in the file: { kind: "slide" | "page" | "sheet" ..., index, ... }.

quote.description: The exact words at that place. They are checked against the file.

target.description: An existing record this evidence supports. Send this or create, not both.

create.description: A new record to create from the evidence: { type, subtype?, fields }.

target.description: Move the evidence to another record.

name.description: The approver's own name, typed by them.

public_url.description: The address approval links start with, for example http://192.168.1.20:4317. Empty clears it.

approval_expiry_days.description: How many days a link lives (1 to 365).

type.description: Record type, e.g. Requirement, Risk, Stakeholder (see GET /api/meta).

status.description: One of the statuses of its type (see GET /api/meta).

phase.description: Lifecycle phase 0-12 the type belongs to.

priority.description: MoSCoW, for types that have it.

rev.description: Revision, goes up with every change. Send it back as expected_rev to avoid overwriting someone else.

LegacyItem.description: A record. Besides these fields it carries the fields of its type (statement, owner, ...).

_suspect.description: A record it depends on changed after it was last reviewed.

LegacyItemListed.description: LegacyItem plus these computed flags (underscore fields).

source.description: Record id the link starts at.

state.description: valid, or suspect when one end changed.

suspect.description: Why it is flagged, or null.

other.description: The record at the other end.

upstream.description: Records this one depends on (up to 3 levels).

downstream.description: Records that depend on this one (up to 3 levels).

items.description: Quotes in uploaded documents that back this record.

offenderCount.description: How many records fail it (offenders lists at most 8).

sig.description: Short fingerprint of what the checks show. Send it back as expected_sig when deciding; a changed picture is refused with 409 stale_gate.

summary.description: Counts: must/should by status, evaluated, passed, failed, pending, waived, readiness.

items.description: Decisions that may be made now.

link.description: Link to send to the approver (only while waiting).

items.description: Record ids it is attached to.

code.description: Machine-readable code, e.g. validation_failed, not_found, role_required, stale_edit.

details.description: Extra detail, e.g. field errors for validation_failed.

requestId.description: Same value as the X-Request-Id response header; quote it when reporting a problem.
